topics: p95 latency targets for streaming chat
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
questions: What p95 is realistic for 1-2k concurrent streams at 512 token context?
How much burst capacity is available on Hosted without moving to Dedicated?
How do prefix/KV caching and batching interact with streaming to preserve latency?
What observability hooks are available to show token-level latency and cost?
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Rina Gupta (Cortexo Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Eng Manager), Sofia Martinez (Security Lead)

Summary: brief intake, then deep into streaming/p95 expectations, concurrent user patterns, and what to benchmark. Several side notes about security and POC timelines. Some transcription noise on acronyms (K-V cash, K M S sometimes).

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick intro, i'm maya, i'll be your AE. daniel is our SE, he'll lead the perf bits. rina, do you want to kick off with the goal for today?

[00:18] Rina (Cortexo): yeah thanks maya. so our main ask — we're building a conversational assistant for clinicians, low latency is critical. target p95 for streaming response end-to-end is around 300 to 400ms for short responses, but for longer ones we expect streaming to keep first token p95 < 250ms, then steady token throughput. we also have big burst events — like morning rounds — where we could see 800 to 1,200 concurrent streams for 10-15 minutes.

[00:40] Liam (Cortexo): and to add, average session is 60 to 90 seconds, a lot of short queries but then the occasional long note generation ~700-900 tokens. cost is a factor but performance is higher priority for clinicians.

[01:05] Daniel (Redwood SE): got it. couple clarifying q's: when you say p95 for streaming, do you mean p95 for first byte of stream or p95 for completion? usually teams separate first-token latency vs completion latency because streaming changes how users perceive slowness.

[01:25] Rina: mostly first-token/payload start and also the briskness of subsequent token delivery — we want human-feel without stuttering. so first-byte p95 target 250ms, and sustained token rate such that we don't drop below ~20-30 tokens/sec per stream for longer outputs.

[01:45] Maya: good, that helps. and the concurrency pattern — 800 to 1,200 simultaneous streams in bursts. is steady-state lower?

[01:55] Rina: steady is 150-200, with peaks as mentioned. peaks last 10-20 minutes, maybe twice a day.

[02:10] Daniel: ok, that gives us two operational modes: steady-state with small batch aggregation and burst mode where we need headroom. For Hosted you can often get automated burst capacity but with some limits; Dedicated gives predictable throughput because you reserve GPU pools. Private gives you complete control but adds ops overhead.

[02:35] Liam: brief question about streaming + batching — does batching hurt first-token latency? we've seen in-house setups where batching introduced 100-200ms extra which killed the UX.

[02:48] Daniel: good point. our runtime supports continuous batching which tries to avoid delaying first token; we use immediate scheduling for streaming paths and can favor latency over throughput. for Dedicated you can tune batching windows aggressively or effectively disable batching for first token short-circuit. there's also prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts which can return sub-50ms in some cases, though real numbers vary.

[03:10] Rina: when you say KV cache — is that a warm cache per model variant or shared? we've got a lot of slightly customized prompt templates per clinic.

[03:22] Daniel: it's per model version and can be tuned by keying on the prompt prefix. small variations reduce hit rate; we recommend normalizing prompt prefixes for caching. also note sometimes the transcriber shows K-V cash — it's actually KV cache.

[03:40] Sofia (Security): quick security interjection — from compliance side we need SOC 2, SSO via SAML, audit logs for every request, and KMS support for key control. can you confirm Redwood's posture here?

[03:55] Maya: yes, we have SOC2, SAML SSO integrations, audit logs in console, and we support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Private deployments and some Dedicated offerings. we'll send the security pack after the call.

[04:08] Sofia: also data residency — some records must stay in eu-west. can you do region pinning?

[04:15] Daniel: yes region pinning is supported on Hosted within our EU region, and Dedicated/Private gives you full control. there can be tradeoffs in latency depending on where clients are.

[04:30] Liam: about benchmark methodology — what would you run to validate p95 and token/sec claims?

[04:38] Daniel: we typically do three tiers: 1) synthetic microbenchmarks for per-token latency across a few sequence lengths; 2) a replay of your anonymized traffic to measure tail behavior and cache hit rates; 3) a soak test under burst windows to observe autoscaling behavior and failovers. for streaming we instrument first-token latency separately and measure tokens/sec distribution.

[05:05] Rina: timeline for a POC? we want results within 3 weeks ideally.

[05:12] Maya: reasonable — we can do a two-week Dedicated sizing POC if infra is available, plus a couple days for baseline microbenchmarks. initial deliverables: benchmark plan, cost estimate, and security package.

[05:30] Liam: curious — what hardware are you recommending for our profile? we're okay with A100s but want cost-effective mix.

[05:38] Daniel: for low p95 streaming and high concurrency, a cluster of 4 x A100s per shard is typical for the workloads you described, using a quantized model variant for cost-savings on steady state. we can also look at newer memory-optimized GPUs if we need higher token/sec. Dedicated can reserve those nodes; Hosted may route across similar hardware but you don't reserve capacity.

[06:05] Rina: and fallback strategies? if Dedicated runs out of capacity during an unforeseen spike, do you have cross-region or lighter model fallbacks?

[06:15] Maya: yes we have routing policies and model variants for graceful degradation — e.g. fall back to a faster quantized variant or to a regional Hosted pool. we can also set canary rollout policies to avoid sudden regressions.

[06:30] Daniel: experiment idea — keep first-token served from a cached prompt prefix where possible, then stream remaining tokens from model. this reduces perceived latency a lot. also continuous KV caching can reduce cost and tokens generated.

[06:55] Rina: how do you measure and report p95 with streaming? in our metrics we need user-visible p95 and an internal server p95.

[07:05] Daniel: we expose token-level traces and per-request timeline in the Console. we can export per-token latencies, p50/p95/p99 for first-byte, and for completion. we'll include a sample dashboard.

[07:20] Sofia: on encryption — can we hold keys in our HSM and only provide pointers to Redwood?

[07:28] Maya: for Private yes, for Dedicated there are options to integrate customer KMS/HSM, for Hosted we do offer customer-managed key integrations depending on contract. we'll detail tradeoffs in the security pack.

[07:45] Liam: any rough cost delta between Hosted bursts vs Dedicated reserved for our peak profile?

[07:54] Maya: rough ballpark — Hosted with burst will be higher per-token during sustained peaks because of on-demand pricing; Dedicated has a fixed monthly commit which is cheaper at scale but requires commitment. we'll include a modeled cost comparison in the pricing snapshot.

[08:10] Rina: for the replay test, we'll need guidance on anonymization. can you provide a template?

[08:18] Daniel: yes we'll send a scrub template. ideally you replace PHI, and we only need prompt texts and timing. please also include a representative distribution of lengths.

[08:35] Maya: ok quick recap and owners: we'll send benchmark plan + pricing + security pack; cortexo provides sample traffic and prompt families; daniel will demo streaming pacing; schedule POC kickoff.

[08:52] Rina: sounds good. one more note — for internal buy-in we need a short doc showing how p95 improvements map to clinician task completion time. can redwood help with a slide or two?

[09:05] Maya: yes we can help with an outcomes slide. we'll add that to the next deliverable.

[09:18] Sofia: timeline check — if you send packs early next week we can aim for POC late feb.

[09:25] Maya: we'll target that. thanks everyone.

[09:30] (call ends, few participants drop)
